hook_text: Seventeen bags, thirty-three metres of tube, eight days, three trips, plus ten percent twice. That is a tender price you can defend.
clip_script: A budget is an estimate with rules. Materials, labour, transport, allowances, total. Quantities from your drawing: ramp 1.3 cubic metres, landing, stairs, kerb, about 2.3 in all, so 17 bags of cement, as sold. Rails 19 metres plus posts 14, 33 metres of galvanised tube, or the fabricator's quote on one line. A bricklayer and two workers for 8 days. Deliveries. Round up to what you can buy: 22.4 bags is 23, 19 metres is four lengths. Add 10 percent for waste, 10 percent for surprises. Then check it: redo the maths, compare with town prices, look at the shares. Save by choosing a cheaper layout, never by shortening the ramp or cutting the contingency. Every line, anyone can check.
visual_style: Whiteboard budget sheet with five section headings filling line by line; quantities flowing from a small drawing; a calculator check tick; a crossed-out shortened ramp.
mood: Honest, organised, ready for the board.
pacing: Shape, quantities, rounding, allowances, three checks, honest savings.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and round up a shopping list to the units a shop actually sells.
